newsitem.title: UK: Wealthy Names leader seeks ruling seat at Lloyd's.
newsitem.headline: Wealthy Names leader seeks ruling seat at Lloyd's.

text.p: A senior member of a group representing some of the wealthiest individuals backing Lloyd's of London is mounting an attempt to win a seat on the British insurance market's eighteen strong ruling council.

Sir William Arbuthnot, deputy chairman of the High Premium Group of Names, as individual investors are called, has been nominated along with four others for the one vacancy on six seats which are allotted to external members, Lloyd's said. Elections to Lloyd's ruling council are held annually and the ballot which closes on December 18 will be the fifteenth since the council was established by the Lloyd's Act of 1982.

Two seats for external members became available as terms of office expired for Jonathan Agnew, the chairman of Lloyd's largest corporate investor LIMIT, and David James, the chairman and chief executive of Eagle Trust.
Agnew was renominated for the seat allocated to represent corporate capital and, because no other candidate stood, has been re-elected.

This makes Arbuthnot's candidacy for the other external seat significant as the High Premium Group, which has several hundred members, strongly maintains that the interests of individual as opposed to corporate investors should be protected.
Corporate capital providers have increased their presence at Lloyd's within the last few years and now support thirty percent of the insurance market's 10 billion stg underwriting capacity.
They invest with limited liability. Names have unlimited liability and many of the wealthiest want Lloyd's to keep this.

Lloyd's has said it will not dictate the balance between the two ways of investing, but momentum is gathering to introduce ways for Names to convert as corporate capital more closely aligns itself with the underwriting agents.

James is eligible for re-election and has stood again along with Sir Adam Ridley, deputy chairman of the Association of Lloyd's Members (ALM), Peter Nutting, former council member and founder of the Outhwaite Names action group, and Dr Julian West.

Another external member's seat is due to become vacant at the end of March next year when Michael Deeny, chairman of the Gooda Walker Names action group, steps down followiong his appointment as a director to the board of Equitas, the Lloyd's reinsurance vehicle. The second highest vote winner fills this.
Four candidates have been put forward for two vacancies on the six seats for working members. These are Ian Agnew, David Robson, James Sinclair, and Brian Smith.
